rationale: Ezekiel says He will lead the people beneath the rod and bring them in by number. Leviticus describes cattle and sheep passing under the staff in the count for the tithe. The legal animal-counting image illuminates the source's wording without replacing it with an unstated bond-of-covenant clause.
source_text: I will lead you beneath My rod and bring you in by number,

target_units.text: And every tithe of cattle and sheep, and everything that comes under the staff in the count—the tenth shall be holy unto the Lord.

relationship: related exclusion of rebels from entering Israel's land
rationale: Ezekiel says the impious will be brought from their sojourning land but will not enter Israel's land. Numbers excludes the grumbling generation from the promised land while distinguishing its children and named faithful exceptions. The sources describe different stages, but departure without eventual entry is the specific shared judgment.
source_text: and select from you the impious and those who have revolted, for I will bring them out of their sojourning, but they will not enter Israel’s land. You will recognize that I am the Lord.

target_units.text: Say to them, I live, says the Lord: I will certainly do to you just as you have spoken into My ears.
In this wilderness your bodies shall fall, with your entire registration and those of you counted from twenty years old and upward who grumbled against Me.
You shall certainly not enter the land over which I stretched out My hand to settle you upon it, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
And I will bring into the land the children whom you said would become plunder, and they shall inherit the land from which you turned away.
And your bodies shall fall in this wilderness.

relationship: related rejection of corrupt worship and command to remove evil practices
rationale: Ezekiel commands removal of practices and says they will no longer profane God's holy name through gifts and practices. Isaiah rejects corrupted offerings and festivals and commands cleansing and removal of evil. Ezekiel's actual command is not rendered as permission to serve idols.
source_text: And you, house of Israel, thus says the Lord, the Lord: Each of you, remove his practices! After these things, if you are not listening to Me, you will no longer profane My holy name with your gifts and practices.

target_units.text: you will no longer continue. If you bring fine flour, it is futile. Incense is an abomination to Me. Your new moons and sabbaths and a great day I cannot endure; fasting and idleness,
and your new moons and your festivals My soul hates. You have become more than enough for Me; I will no longer let your sins go.
Whenever you stretch your hands toward Me, I will turn My eyes away from you. Even if you multiply supplication, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.
Wash yourselves, become clean. Remove the evils from your souls, before My eyes. Stop your evil deeds.

relationship: close accepted worship on God's holy mountain
rationale: Ezekiel promises that Israel will serve God on His holy mountain, with offerings accepted. Isaiah promises the attached foreigners joy on His holy mountain and acceptance of their sacrifices. The common mountain and acceptance are explicit, while the named worshipping groups differ.
source_text: For upon My holy mountain, upon a high mountain, says the Lord, the Lord, there the whole house of Israel will serve Me to the end. There I will accept, and there I will attend to your firstfruits and the firstfruits of your separations, with all your holy things.

target_units.text: And the foreigners attached to the Lord, to serve Him and love the Lord’s name, to become His male and female slaves, and all those keeping My Sabbaths from profanation and holding fast to My covenant—

I will bring them into My holy mountain and make them rejoice in My house of prayer. Their whole burnt offerings and sacrifices will be acceptable on My altar, for My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations,”

relationship: close gathering accompanied by divine sanctification before the nations
rationale: Ezekiel joins gathering the scattered people with God's being sanctified in them before the peoples. The later oracle similarly joins sanctification before the nations' eyes with gathering from countries. It does not include this source's fragrant-aroma wording.
source_text: As a fragrant aroma I will accept you when I bring you out from the peoples and receive you from the countries where you were scattered. I will be sanctified among you before the eyes of the peoples.

target_units.text: I will sanctify My great name, profaned among the nations, which you profaned among them. The nations will know that I am the Lord when I am sanctified in you before their eyes.
I will take you out of the nations, gather you out of all the lands and bring you into your own land.

relationship: related application of fragrant-aroma imagery to people before God
rationale: God says He will accept the gathered people as a fragrant aroma. Paul describes the ministering we as Christ's fragrance to God among both those being saved and those perishing. The human-fragrance imagery corresponds, without identifying the restored people with the apostolic speakers or equating all the outcomes.
source_text: As a fragrant aroma I will accept you when I bring you out from the peoples and receive you from the countries where you were scattered. I will be sanctified among you before the eyes of the peoples.

target_units.text: But thanks be to God, who always leads us in triumph in Christ and makes known through us the aroma of the knowledge of Him in every place.
For we are Christ’s fragrance to God among those being saved and among those perishing:
to the one an aroma from death to death, but to the other an aroma from life to life. And who is sufficient for these things?

relationship: close promise of the land pledged to the fathers by an extended hand
rationale: Ezekiel recalls bringing Israel into the land pledged to the fathers with God's raised hand. Exodus likewise promises the land over which He stretched out His hand, expressly naming Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. The source expressly promises recognition; Exodus concludes I am the Lord, with the preceding 6:7 also promising recognition.
source_text: You will recognize that I am the Lord when I bring you into Israel’s land, into the land for which I raised My hand to give it to your fathers.

target_units.text: I will bring you into the land concerning which I stretched out My hand to give it to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I will give it to you as an inheritance. I am the Lord.’”

relationship: close remembrance of defiled ways with differing responses
rationale: Both passages say the restored people will remember their evil ways and practices. This source says they will beat their faces over their evils; the later passage says they will feel disgust for their lawless deeds. The bodily action is not replaced with the target's wording of disgust.
source_text: There you will remember your ways and your practices by which you were being defiled; you will beat your faces over all your evils.

target_units.text: You will remember your evil ways and practices that were not good, and feel disgust before them at your lawless deeds and abominations.

relationship: close divine action explained by concern for the holy name
rationale: Ezekiel connects God's dealings with the people and their recognition of Him to avoiding profanation of His name. The later oracle expressly says He acts for His holy name, profaned among the nations, rather than for Israel's sake. The latter explicit contrast clarifies the comparison without replacing the source's own syntax.
source_text: You will recognize that I am the Lord when I deal thus with you so that My name may not be profaned according to your evil ways and corrupt practices, says the Lord.’”

target_units.text: Therefore say to Israel’s house, ‘Thus says the Lord: I am not acting for you, house of Israel, but because of My holy name, which you profaned among the nations where you entered.

relationship: related paired green-and-dry wood imagery in a warning of judgment
rationale: Ezekiel describes fire consuming both green and dry trees. Jesus asks what will happen with dry wood if such things are done with green wood. The paired kinds of wood correspond, while Luke does not expressly name a forest fire in this saying.
source_text: and say to the Nageb forest, ‘Hear the Lord’s word! Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am kindling a fire within you. It will devour every green tree and every dry tree in you. The kindled flame will not be quenched, and every face from east to north will be burned by it.

target_units.text: For if they do these things with the green wood, what will happen with the dry?”

relationship: close divine fire that will not be extinguished
rationale: Ezekiel says all flesh will recognize that God kindled the fire and that it will not be extinguished. Jeremiah likewise announces God kindling a fire that consumes Jerusalem's quarters and is not extinguished. The source's forest imagery differs from the target's gates and quarters.
source_text: All flesh will recognize that I, the Lord, have kindled it, and it will not be quenched.’”

target_units.text: And if you do not listen to Me to consecrate the Sabbath day, not lifting burdens and not entering Jerusalem’s gates on the Sabbath day, I will kindle fire in her gates, and it will devour Jerusalem’s quarters and not be extinguished.

relationship: related description and divine command of prophetic parable speech
rationale: The prophet reports people calling his speech a parable. Earlier he was expressly commanded to tell a story and speak a parable to Israel. The connection concerns the stated mode of speech without deciding whether the reported audience meant its remark as a rejection.
source_text: I said, “By no means, Lord, Lord! They say to me, ‘Is this not a parable being spoken?’”

target_units.text: “Son of man, tell a story and speak a parable to the house of Israel,

relationship: close face-setting toward Jerusalem in a prophetic siege setting
rationale: Ezekiel is commanded to set his face toward Jerusalem and prophesy against Israel's land. The earlier siege sign requires drawing Jerusalem on a brick and preparing his face against it. The target supplies a physical sign that this source does not separately command.
source_text: “Therefore prophesy, son of man; set your face firmly toward Jerusalem, look toward their holy places, and prophesy against Israel’s land,

target_units.text: “And you, son of man, take a brick, set it before your face, and draw upon it a city—Jerusalem;
lay siege to it, build forward defenses against it, throw up a palisade against it, set camps against it, and arrange missile positions all around.
Take an iron pan and place it as an iron wall between you and the city. Prepare your face against it; it will be besieged, and you will besiege it. This is a sign for the sons of Israel.

relationship: related divine sword employed in judgment
rationale: God draws His dagger against the unjust and lawless. Deuteronomy describes His sharpened sword, hand taking hold of judgment and repayment to enemies. The target's enemies are not substituted for the source's exact unjust-and-lawless wording.
source_text: and say to Israel’s land, ‘Behold, I am against you. I will draw My dagger from its sheath and destroy from you the unjust and the lawless.

target_units.text: For I will sharpen My sword as lightning, and My hand shall lay hold of judgment; and I will repay a penalty unto the enemies, and unto them that hate Me will I repay.

relationship: close divine sword judgment extending to all flesh
rationale: Ezekiel says God's dagger goes against all flesh from east to north. Isaiah likewise speaks of the Lord's sword judging all flesh. The target adds fire and the whole earth; neither supplies Ezekiel's particular directional wording.
source_text: Because I will destroy from you the unjust and the lawless, so My dagger will come out of its sheath against all flesh from east to north.

target_units.text: For by the Lord’s fire all the earth will be judged, and by His sword all flesh; many will be wounded by the Lord.

relationship: related groaning and afflicted loins in response to a harsh vision
rationale: Ezekiel is commanded to groan with broken loins and pain. Isaiah's speaker groans and describes loins filled with weakness and labor pains after a harsh vision. The target's childbirth comparison is not inserted into Ezekiel's instruction.
source_text: And you, son of man, groan deeply with your loins broken; groan in pains before their eyes.

target_units.text: and harsh vision was announced to me. The faithless person deals faithlessly, and the lawless person acts lawlessly. The Elamites are against me, and Persian envoys come against me. Now I will groan and comfort myself.
Therefore my loins filled with weakness, and labor pains seized me like a woman giving birth. I did wrong by not hearing; I strove not to see.

relationship: close bodily collapse at announced judgment
rationale: Ezekiel predicts broken hearts and paralyzed hands when the report arrives. Isaiah's Babylon oracle describes slackened hands, cowardly souls and distress. The correspondence concerns disabled strength and fear, not an equivalence between Ezekiel's moist thighs and wording absent from Isaiah.
source_text: If they say to you, ‘Why are you groaning?’ say, ‘Because of the message, for it is coming. Every heart will be shattered, all hands will be paralyzed, all flesh and every spirit will expire, and all thighs will be defiled with moisture. Behold, it is coming and will happen, says the Lord, the Lord.’”

target_units.text: Therefore every hand will slacken, and every human soul grow cowardly;
the envoys will be troubled, and labor pains will hold them like those of a woman giving birth. They will lament to one another and be distraught, and change their face as to flame.

relationship: related preparation of a divine sword for judgment
rationale: The prophetic command calls for the sword to be sharpened and enraged. The psalm describes the righteous divine judge polishing His sword if the addressees do not return. The psalm supplies an express conditional return clause absent from this source unit.
source_text: “Son of man, prophesy and say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Say: Sword, sword, be sharpened and enraged,

target_units.text: God is a righteous judge, strong and patient, not bringing wrath every day.
If you do not return, He will polish His sword; He bent His bow and prepared it,

relationship: close gleaming or lightning-like sword prepared for judgment
rationale: Ezekiel commands sharpening the sword to gleam for slaughter. Deuteronomy describes God sharpening His sword like lightning to take judgment in hand. The target does not explain the source's unusual command concerning every tree.
source_text: so that you may slaughter victims. Be sharpened to become gleaming. Ready for paralysis, slaughter! Disdain; thrust away every tree.

target_units.text: For I will sharpen My sword as lightning, and My hand shall lay hold of judgment; and I will repay a penalty unto the enemies, and unto them that hate Me will I repay.

relationship: related preparation of deadly weapons
rationale: Ezekiel says the sharpened sword is ready to be placed in the piercer's hand. The psalm describes the sword, prepared bow and instruments of death. The shared readiness for judgment does not make the sword and bow identical or identify the source's unnamed piercer.
source_text: He gave it ready for his hand to grasp. The sword has been sharpened; it is ready to be put into the hand of one who pierces.

target_units.text: If you do not return, He will polish His sword; He bent His bow and prepared it,
and in it He prepared instruments of death; He fashioned His arrows for those being burned.

relationship: close prophetic hand gesture accompanying announced judgment
rationale: Ezekiel is commanded to cry, wail and strike his hand because the sword has come among Israel's people and leaders. The earlier command likewise includes clapping the hand while announcing sword, death and famine for Israel's abominations. Its foot-stamping and spoken exclamation are additional actions.
source_text: Cry aloud and wail, son of man, for it has come among My people, among all Israel’s leaders. They will sojourn upon a sword; it has come among My people. Therefore strike upon your hand.

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord: Clap your hand, stamp your foot, and say, “Aha! Aha!” over all the abominations of the house of Israel; they will fall by sword, death and famine.

relationship: close hand-clapping within a prophetic judgment announcement
rationale: The prophet is told to prophesy and strike hand upon hand while speaking about the sword. The earlier oracle also commands a hand clap in an announcement of Israel's downfall. This supports the performed gesture without resolving the source's difficult third-sword expression.
source_text: And you, son of man, prophesy and strike hand upon hand, and double the sword. The third sword of the wounded is the great sword of the wounded, and it will terrify them,

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord: Clap your hand, stamp your foot, and say, “Aha! Aha!” over all the abominations of the house of Israel; they will fall by sword, death and famine.

relationship: close divine hand-clapping over the people's judgment
rationale: God says He will clap His hands and release His wrath. The following oracle speaks conditionally of God clapping His hands over the city's bloodshed. The actor is God in both, distinct from commands elsewhere for the prophet to clap.
source_text: I too will strike My hand against My hand and release My wrath. I, the Lord, have spoken.’”

target_units.text: But if I strike My hand against My hand over what you have completed, what you did, and over your bloodshed that occurred within you,

relationship: contrast between Babylonian royal divination and Israel's prohibition
rationale: Babylon's king uses divination at the road junction, including a rod, carved images and a liver. Deuteronomy prohibits divination and says the nations heed it but Israel is not granted that practice. The law does not list the source's three particular implements or imply that the narrative endorses the practice.
source_text: For Babylon’s king will stand upon the ancient road, at the beginning of the two roads, to divine a divination, toss a rod, question the carved images and inspect a liver at his right.

target_units.text: There shall not be found among you one who purifies his son or his daughter by fire, or practises divination, or interprets spoken omens, or observes auguries, or works sorcery,
or chants spells, or is a medium, or observes portents, or inquires of the dead.
For everyone who does these things is an abomination unto the Lord your God; for because of these abominations the Lord shall destroy them from before you.
You shall be perfect before the Lord your God.
For these nations whose possession you inherit hearken unto omens and divinations; but the Lord your God has not granted you so to do.

relationship: related Babylonian preparations for Jerusalem's siege
rationale: The oracle selects Jerusalem for siege works, missile stations and shouting. Jeremiah records Babylon's king and force enclosing Jerusalem with a palisade and building around it. The historical counterpart does not narrate the preceding divination or make every siege feature identical.
source_text: The oracle came against Jerusalem: to set a siege stake, open the mouth in a shout, raise the voice with a cry, set a siege stake against her gates, cast up a mound and build missile stations.

target_units.text: In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his force came against Jerusalem. They enclosed her with a palisade and built around her with squared stones.

relationship: related remembrance of wrongdoing followed by punitive consequences
rationale: Ezekiel says the people recalled their injustices as their impieties were revealed and announces capture. Hosea says God will remember their injustices and punish their sins, in a passage naming Egypt and Assyria. The remembering subjects and the different movements described are preserved.
source_text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Because you recalled your injustices when your impieties were revealed, so that your sins were seen in all your impieties and practices—because you recalled them, in these you will be captured.

target_units.text: Because even if they offer a sacrifice and eat meat, the Lord will not accept them. Now He will remember their injustices and punish their sins. They returned to Egypt and will eat unclean things among the Assyrians.

relationship: same-chapter repeated appointed-day judgment formula
rationale: The profane leader of Israel is addressed as one whose day has arrived in a season of injustice, an end. The Ammon oracle repeats that formulation concerning wounded lawless people. The repeated judgment language links the two sections without identifying their persons as the same.
source_text: And you, profane, lawless leader of Israel, whose day has arrived in a season of injustice—an end!—

target_units.text: in your vain vision and your divining false things, to hand you over upon the necks of the wounded lawless, whose day has arrived in a season of injustice—an end!

relationship: related reversal of high and low with distinct grammatical agents
rationale: This source says its addressee removed the tiara, put on the crown, lowered the high and raised the low. The cedar oracle says God lowers the high tree and raises the low. The shared reversal does not turn this source into a command to remove the crown or make its second-person acts God's first-person acts.
source_text: thus says the Lord: You removed the tiara and put on the crown. This will not be such. You lowered the high and raised the low.

target_units.text: All the plain’s trees will know that I am the Lord who lowers a high tree, raises a low tree, dries a green tree and makes a dry tree flourish. I, the Lord, have spoken and will act.”

relationship: related expectation of a future rightful recipient in a royal setting
rationale: Ezekiel looks toward the one to whom it belongs, to whom God will hand it over. Genesis says the ruler from Judah will not fail until the things reserved for him come, followed by the expectation of nations. The future royal language is related without claiming the passages give an identical name or wording.
source_text: Injustice, injustice I will make it! Nor will this be such until the one comes to whom it belongs, and I will hand it over to him.

target_units.text: “A ruler shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until the things reserved for him come; and he shall be the expectation of nations.

relationship: close judgment oracles concerning Ammon and its hostile response
rationale: Ezekiel's sword oracle expressly concerns Ammon's sons and their reproach. The later oracle condemns their rejoicing at the profanation and devastation of Israel and announces punishment. It specifies a hostile response not fully narrated in this source unit.
source_text: And you, son of man, prophesy and say, ‘Thus says the Lord concerning the sons of Ammon and their reproach.’ Say, ‘Sword, sword, drawn for victims and drawn for complete destruction, arise so that you may gleam,

target_units.text: “Son of man, set your face firmly against the sons of Ammon and prophesy against them,

and say to Ammon’s sons, ‘Hear the Lord’s word! Thus says the Lord: Because you rejoiced over My holy things when they were profaned, over Israel’s land when it was devastated, and over Judah’s house when they went into captivity,

therefore behold, I am handing you to the sons of Kedem as an inheritance. They will camp with their equipment in you and set their dwellings in you. They will eat your fruits and drink your richness.
I will make Ammon’s city pastures for camels, and Ammon’s sons a pasture for sheep. You will recognize that I am the Lord.
For thus says the Lord: Because you clapped your hand and made noise with your foot, and rejoiced from your soul over Israel’s land,

therefore I will stretch My hand against you, give you to plunder among the nations, utterly destroy you from the peoples and make you perish from the countries with destruction. You will recognize that I am the Lord.’

relationship: close false vision and vain divination brought under judgment
rationale: The source names vain vision and false divination within the Ammon judgment. The earlier oracle likewise condemns prophets seeing false things and uttering vain divinations and announces God's opposition. The different addressees and penalties are not merged.
source_text: in your vain vision and your divining false things, to hand you over upon the necks of the wounded lawless, whose day has arrived in a season of injustice—an end!

target_units.text: They see false things and divine vain things, those who say, ‘The Lord says,’ although the Lord has not sent them; and they began to establish a word.
Have you not seen a false vision and spoken vain divinations?
Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Because your words are false and your divinations vain, therefore behold, I am against you, says the Lord,

and I will stretch out My hand against the prophets who see false things and utter vain things. They will not belong to My people’s instruction, nor be written in the register of the house of Israel, nor enter Israel’s land. They will know that I am the Lord.

relationship: related divine anger expressed as consuming fire
rationale: God says He will blow upon the addressee with the fire of His anger. Isaiah describes the anger of His wrath consuming like fire. The target supports the fiery-anger image without supplying a breath clause or the source's barbarian destroyers.
source_text: and pour My anger upon you. I will blow upon you with the fire of My anger and hand you into the hands of barbarian men devising destruction.

target_units.text: Behold, the Lord’s name comes after a long time, wrath burning. His lips’ utterance comes with glory, an utterance full of anger, and the anger of His wrath will consume like fire.

relationship: close announced destruction of Ammon among the peoples
rationale: The Ammon oracle predicts fiery destruction and no further remembrance. The later oracle likewise promises to destroy Ammon from the peoples and countries. Its description of plunder and removal is not replaced with the source's exact fire-and-blood details.
source_text: You will be food in fire; your blood will be in the midst of your land. There certainly will be no remembrance of you, for I, the Lord, have spoken.’”

target_units.text: therefore I will stretch My hand against you, give you to plunder among the nations, utterly destroy you from the peoples and make you perish from the countries with destruction. You will recognize that I am the Lord.’

relationship: close prophetic indictment of a city of bloodshed
rationale: Ezekiel is commanded to judge the city of bloodshed and expose its lawlessness. Nahum similarly addresses a city of bloodshed, adding falsehood and injustice. Nahum's surrounding oracle names Nineveh, so the two cities are not identified with each other.
source_text: “And you, son of man, will you judge the city of bloodshed? Display all her lawless deeds to her,

target_units.text: O city of bloodshed, wholly false, full of injustice! Prey will not be touched.

relationship: related civic or national defilement followed by judgment
rationale: The city sheds blood and makes reflections that defile it as its time approaches. The later oracle describes Israel's defiling the land through its ways, idols and uncleannesses, followed by wrath and scattering. That target does not expressly repeat the bloodshed clause in this edition.
source_text: and say, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: O city shedding blood within her so that her time may come, making reflections against herself to defile herself!

target_units.text: “Son of man, Israel’s house lived upon their land and defiled it by their way, their idols and their uncleannesses. Their way before Me became like the uncleanness of a woman sitting apart.
I poured My wrath upon them
and scattered them among the nations and winnowed them into the countries. I judged them according to their way and their sin.

relationship: related public disgrace among the nations
rationale: God makes the guilty city a reproach and an object of mockery among nations and countries. Deuteronomy warns that the displaced people will become a riddle, parable and tale among nations. The shared public example of judgment preserves the target's wording rather than replacing it with mockery.
source_text: Through their blood that you shed you have transgressed, and through your reflections that you made you were being defiled. You brought your days near and brought the season of your years. Therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations and a mockery to all the countries

target_units.text: The Lord lead you, and your rulers whom you shall set over yourself, unto a nation which neither you nor your fathers have known; and there you shall serve other gods, wood and stone.
And there you shall become a riddle, and a parable, and a tale among all the nations whither the Lord shall lead you.

relationship: related humiliation of the sinful city before observers
rationale: Those near and far mock the city's uncleanness and lawlessness. Lamentations describes Jerusalem's enemies laughing at her deportation, former admirers humbling her and her uncleanness exposed. It does not specify Ezekiel's near-and-far groups.
source_text: near you and far away from you. They will mock you: “Unclean, the famous one, abundant in lawless deeds!”

target_units.text: Jerusalem remembered the days of her humiliation and rejection, all her desired things from ancient days. When her people fell into the oppressor’s hands and no one helped her, her enemies saw her and laughed at her deportation.
Jerusalem has sinned grievously; therefore she has come into upheaval. All who glorified her humbled her, for they saw her shame. She too groaned and turned backward.
Her uncleanness is at her feet; she did not remember her last things. He brought her down exceedingly; there is no one to comfort her. See, Lord, my humiliation, for the enemy has grown great!

relationship: contrast between reviling parents and the command to honor them
rationale: Ezekiel accuses the city of reviling father and mother. Exodus commands honoring father and mother, attaching a promise of well-being and long life. This target addresses the parental clause, distinct from the source's treatment of vulnerable outsiders.
source_text: They reviled father and mother in you and dealt unjustly with the sojourner in you. They oppressed the orphan and widow in you.

target_units.text: Honour your father and your mother, that it may be well with you, and that your days may be long upon the good land which the Lord your God gives you.

relationship: close violations concerning the sojourner, orphan and widow
rationale: Ezekiel accuses the people of injustice toward the sojourner and oppression of orphan and widow. Exodus prohibits wronging the foreigner and harming widow or orphan, warning of God's hearing their cry. The three protected groups correspond directly.
source_text: They reviled father and mother in you and dealt unjustly with the sojourner in you. They oppressed the orphan and widow in you.

target_units.text: And you shall not ill-treat a resident foreigner, neither shall you afflict him; for you were resident foreigners in the land of Egypt.
You shall not mistreat any widow or orphan.
But if you afflict them, and they cry aloud to Me, I will surely listen to their voice,
I will be angry with wrath and kill you with the sword. Your wives will become widows and your children orphans.

relationship: close inverse of the paired Sabbath-and-holy-things command
rationale: Ezekiel accuses the people of despising God's holy things and profaning His Sabbaths. Leviticus pairs keeping His Sabbaths with revering His holy things. The accusation directly reverses both duties in that command.
source_text: They despised My holy things and profaned My Sabbaths in you.

target_units.text: You shall keep My Sabbaths and revere My holy things. I am the Lord.

relationship: related association of robbery with bloodshed
rationale: Ezekiel identifies robbers in the city who shed blood. Proverbs depicts an invitation to bloodshed and seizure of costly property and warns against those paths. The target supports that violent robbery clause, not Ezekiel's separate accusation of mountain eating.
source_text: Robbers are in you in order to shed blood in you. They ate upon the mountains in you; they committed unholy acts within you.

target_units.text: Son, do not let ungodly men lead you astray; do not agree if they invite you, saying,
Come with us; share in bloodshed. Let us hide a righteous man in the earth unjustly;
let us swallow him alive like Hades and remove his memory from the earth.
Let us seize his costly property and fill our houses with spoils.
Cast your lot among us; let us all obtain a common purse, and let there be one moneybag for us.
Do not walk in the way with them; turn your foot away from their paths,
for their feet run toward evil, and they are quick to shed blood.

relationship: close violation concerning the father's nakedness
rationale: Ezekiel says the father's shame is uncovered in the city. Leviticus expressly prohibits uncovering the father's nakedness and explains the prohibition regarding his wife. The source does not separately name the particular woman in this clause.
source_text: They uncovered a father’s shame in you, and they violated a woman sitting apart in uncleanness in you.

target_units.text: You shall not uncover your father’s nakedness or your mother’s nakedness. She is your mother; you shall not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife; it is your father’s nakedness.

relationship: close prohibition concerning a woman in menstrual separation
rationale: Ezekiel accuses the people of violating a woman during her menstrual separation. Leviticus forbids approaching a woman in that separation to uncover her nakedness. This is distinct from the source's preceding paternal-shame accusation.
source_text: They uncovered a father’s shame in you, and they violated a woman sitting apart in uncleanness in you.

target_units.text: And you shall not approach a woman in separation for her uncleanness to uncover her nakedness.

relationship: close prohibition against adultery with a neighbor's wife
rationale: Ezekiel accuses one person of unlawful conduct with his neighbor's wife. Leviticus expressly prohibits intercourse with that wife and consequent defilement. The source goes on to list separate kinship offenses.
source_text: Each acted lawlessly with his neighbor’s wife; each defiled his daughter-in-law with impiety; each violated his sister, his father’s daughter, in you.

target_units.text: And you shall not lie with your neighbour’s wife to emit semen and become defiled through her.

relationship: close named kinship prohibitions involving sister and daughter-in-law
rationale: Ezekiel names defilement of a daughter-in-law and violation of a sister who is the father's daughter. The selected laws explicitly prohibit uncovering a paternal sister and a daughter-in-law, among other relatives. The target's additional kinship categories are not assigned to this source unit.
source_text: Each acted lawlessly with his neighbor’s wife; each defiled his daughter-in-law with impiety; each violated his sister, his father’s daughter, in you.

target_units.text: The nakedness of your sister, from your father or from your mother, born at home or born outside: you shall not uncover her nakedness.
The nakedness of your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter, you shall not uncover their nakedness, for it is your nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife’s daughter. She is your sister by the same father; you shall not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s sister; she is your father’s close relative.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister; she is your mother’s close relative.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s brother, and you shall not go in to his wife. She is your relative.
You shall not uncover your daughter-in-law’s nakedness. She is your son’s wife; you shall not uncover her nakedness.

relationship: close prohibition against accepting payment for bloodshed
rationale: Ezekiel condemns taking gifts in order to shed blood. Deuteronomy pronounces a curse on taking a bribe to kill an innocent life. The target explicitly specifies innocence; the source also lists lending abuses and forgetting God.
source_text: They took gifts in you in order to shed blood; they took interest and increase in you. You brought your evil in oppression to its full completion, but you forgot Me, says the Lord.

target_units.text: Cursed is he who takes a bribe to slay an innocent life. And all the people shall say: So be it.

relationship: close violation of the interest-and-increase prohibition
rationale: Ezekiel names taking interest and increase among the city's offenses. Leviticus prohibits those practices toward the impoverished brother. This legal connection addresses the lending clause rather than the distinct bribe-for-bloodshed charge.
source_text: They took gifts in you in order to shed blood; they took interest and increase in you. You brought your evil in oppression to its full completion, but you forgot Me, says the Lord.

target_units.text: You shall take no interest or increase from him, and you shall fear your God; I am the Lord; and your brother shall live with you.
You shall not give him your silver at interest or give your food for an increase.

relationship: close divine hand-clapping in judgment
rationale: God speaks conditionally of clapping His hands over the source city's deeds and bloodshed. The preceding sword oracle likewise has God clap His hands and release His wrath. The divine actor and judgment gesture are shared without inserting the target's sword into this source unit.
source_text: But if I strike My hand against My hand over what you have completed, what you did, and over your bloodshed that occurred within you,

target_units.text: I too will strike My hand against My hand and release My wrath. I, the Lord, have spoken.’”

relationship: close rhetorical challenge about enduring divine anger
rationale: Ezekiel asks whether the people's heart and hands can remain strong in the days when God acts. Nahum asks who can stand before His anger or resist His wrath. The target adds rulers melting and rocks being crushed rather than the source's heart-and-hands formulation.
source_text: will your heart hold out? Will your hands prevail in the days when I act within you? I, the Lord, have spoken and will act.

target_units.text: Who will stand before His anger? Who will resist His furious wrath? His fury melts rulers, and rocks were crushed before Him.

relationship: related scattering and eventual removal of uncleanness
rationale: Ezekiel joins scattering among nations with the ending of uncleanness. The later passage recalls scattering, then promises gathering and cleansing by clean water. The comparison preserves those distinct narrated stages rather than asserting that the cleansing mechanism is identical.
source_text: I will scatter you among the nations and disperse you among the countries, and your uncleanness will cease from you.

target_units.text: and scattered them among the nations and winnowed them into the countries. I judged them according to their way and their sin.
They entered the nations where they entered, and profaned My holy name when it was said of them, ‘These are the Lord’s people, and they have left His land.’
I spared them because of My holy name, which Israel’s house profaned among the nations where they entered.
Therefore say to Israel’s house, ‘Thus says the Lord: I am not acting for you, house of Israel, but because of My holy name, which you profaned among the nations where you entered.
I will sanctify My great name, profaned among the nations, which you profaned among them. The nations will know that I am the Lord when I am sanctified in you before their eyes.
I will take you out of the nations, gather you out of all the lands and bring you into your own land.
I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you will be cleansed from all your uncleannesses and all your idols. I will cleanse you.

relationship: related compromised-metal imagery for a corrupt community
rationale: Israel's house is described as a mixture of copper, iron, tin, lead and silver. Isaiah addresses the corrupt city Zion and calls her silver unapproved. The source does not expressly call its mixture dross, and the target does not list all its metals.
source_text: “Son of man, behold, Israel’s house has become mixed to Me, all of them with copper, iron, tin and lead; it is mixed amid silver.

target_units.text: How the faithful city Zion has become a prostitute, full of judgment, in which righteousness lay at rest, but now murderers!
Your silver is unapproved; your retailers mix the wine with water.

relationship: related metal imagery for the corrupt people facing divine assessment
rationale: God calls the people a mixture and announces gathering them into Jerusalem, following the list of metals. Jeremiah's testing oracle describes the people as bronze and iron and calls them corrupted. The target supports the characterization but does not describe the source's gathering into Jerusalem.
source_text: Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Because all of you became one mixture, therefore I am receiving you into Jerusalem.

target_units.text: I have made you a tester among tested peoples, and you will know Me when I test their way.
All are unheeding, walking crookedly, bronze and iron; all are corrupted.

relationship: related furnace imagery applied to God's dealings with people
rationale: God compares gathering the people in wrath with metals placed in a furnace and melted. Proverbs compares silver and gold tested in a furnace with hearts chosen before the Lord. The source's destructive melting is not simply renamed the target's testing or choosing.
source_text: As silver, copper, iron, tin and lead are received into a furnace to blow fire into it to melt it, so I will receive you in My anger, gather you and melt you,

target_units.text: As silver and gold are tested in a furnace, so hearts are chosen before the Lord.

relationship: related blast associated with divine anger
rationale: Ezekiel says God will blow upon the gathered people with the fire of His wrath and melt them. The psalm describes exposed foundations and springs at the blast of the spirit of God's anger. The shared angry blast produces different explicitly described effects.
source_text: and blow upon you with the fire of My anger, and you will be melted within her.

target_units.text: And the springs of the waters appeared, and the foundations of the inhabited world were uncovered at Thy rebuke, Lord, at the blast of the spirit of Thine anger.

relationship: related divine treatment of people through fire-and-silver imagery
rationale: Ezekiel compares the people melting under wrath with silver melting in a furnace. The psalm says God tried His people by fire as silver and brought them through affliction to refreshment. The target's stated testing and refreshing outcome are not imposed on Ezekiel's wrath oracle.
source_text: As silver is melted within a furnace, so you will be melted within her. You will recognize that I, the Lord, have poured My wrath upon you.’”

target_units.text: For Thou didst test us, God; Thou didst try us by fire as silver is tried by fire.
Thou broughtest us into the trap; Thou didst place afflictions upon our back.
Thou madest human beings mount our heads; we passed through fire and water, and Thou broughtest us out to refreshment.

relationship: related absence of sustaining rain under divine judgment
rationale: Ezekiel calls the land unwetted and without rain on the day of wrath. Deuteronomy's curses describe bronze heaven and dust given instead of rain. The target supplies different atmospheric imagery for the same loss of life-sustaining rainfall.
source_text: “Son of man, say to her, ‘You are a land not wetted, nor did rain come upon you on the day of wrath.

target_units.text: And the heaven above your head shall be bronze, and the earth beneath you iron.
The Lord give dust for the rain of your land; and earth shall descend upon you from heaven, until He wears you away, and until He destroys you.

relationship: close comparison of rulers with roaring lions
rationale: Ezekiel's leaders are like a roaring lion seizing prey and devouring lives. Zephaniah likewise calls the city's rulers roaring lions. The source says leaders, not prophets, and adds unjust payments and multiplied widows.
source_text: Her leaders within her are like roaring lions seizing prey, devouring lives with power, taking payments unjustly, and your widows have multiplied within you.

target_units.text: Her rulers within her are like roaring lions; her judges are like Arabian wolves, leaving nothing for morning.

relationship: close neglect of priestly distinctions prescribed in the law
rationale: Ezekiel accuses priests of failing to distinguish holy from profane and unclean from clean. Leviticus commands precisely these distinctions and instruction of Israel in God's statutes. The source additionally names Sabbath neglect.
source_text: Her priests set aside My law and profaned My holy things. They did not distinguish between holy and profane, nor distinguish between unclean and clean. They covered their eyes from My Sabbaths, and I was profaned among them.

target_units.text: to distinguish between the holy and the profane, and between the unclean and the clean.
And you shall instruct the sons of Israel in all the statutes which the Lord spoke unto them by the hand of Moses.

relationship: close restoration of the priestly duties neglected in the indictment
rationale: The indicted priests fail to teach holy/profane and clean/unclean distinctions and disregard Sabbaths. The later priestly instruction explicitly requires teaching both distinctions and sanctifying Sabbaths. The latter describes prescribed future duties rather than asserting that these indicted priests already fulfilled them.
source_text: Her priests set aside My law and profaned My holy things. They did not distinguish between holy and profane, nor distinguish between unclean and clean. They covered their eyes from My Sabbaths, and I was profaned among them.

target_units.text: They will teach My people the difference between holy and profane, and make known to them the difference between unclean and clean.
In a case involving blood they will stand to decide. They will uphold My judgments and judge My decisions; they will keep My ordinances and My commands at all My festivals, and sanctify My Sabbaths.

relationship: close predatory-wolf imagery for civic authorities
rationale: Ezekiel compares rulers who shed blood for greedy gain with wolves seizing prey. Zephaniah compares judges with Arabian wolves leaving nothing for morning. The offices and the target's qualifier differ, while the predatory civic image corresponds.
source_text: Her rulers within her are like wolves seizing prey to shed blood, so that in greed they may gain more.

target_units.text: Her rulers within her are like roaring lions; her judges are like Arabian wolves, leaving nothing for morning.

relationship: close conjunction of false oracles, coating and an announced fall
rationale: The source says her prophets, coating them, will fall and condemns their vain visions and claims that God spoke when He did not. The earlier oracle combines false claims of divine speech with a coated wall that will fall. The falling prophets and falling wall remain distinct; no unmentioned mortar recipe is supplied.
source_text: Her prophets, coating them, will fall, seeing vain things, divining falsehoods, saying, “Thus says the Lord,” when the Lord has not spoken,

target_units.text: They see false things and divine vain things, those who say, ‘The Lord says,’ although the Lord has not sent them; and they began to establish a word.
Have you not seen a false vision and spoken vain divinations?
Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Because your words are false and your divinations vain, therefore behold, I am against you, says the Lord,

and I will stretch out My hand against the prophets who see false things and utter vain things. They will not belong to My people’s instruction, nor be written in the register of the house of Israel, nor enter Israel’s land. They will know that I am the Lord.
Because they misled My people, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there was no peace, and this one builds a wall, and they coat it—if it is going to fall,

say to those coating it, ‘It will fall.’ There will be a flooding downpour, and I will put stones for hurling into their bonds, and they will fall; there will be an upending wind, and it will be split.

relationship: close prohibition against oppressing the poor and outsider
rationale: The source charges oppression of the poor and needy and injustice to the sojourner. Zechariah commands righteous judgment and forbids oppressing the poor and newcomer, also naming widow and orphan. The source's particular exploited groups are directly covered.
source_text: oppressing the people of the land unjustly and seizing plunder, oppressing the poor and needy and not dealing justly with the sojourner.

target_units.text: “Thus says the Lord Almighty: Render righteous judgment; show mercy and compassion, each to his brother.
Do not oppress widow, orphan, newcomer or poor person, and let no one harbor resentment for his brother’s wrong in your hearts.”

relationship: close search for a just person in order to spare the community
rationale: God says He sought someone conducting himself rightly and standing wholly before Him so that He would not destroy the land, but found none. Jeremiah commands a search through Jerusalem for one doing justice and seeking faithfulness, with mercy promised if found. The target states the condition rather than the source's explicit failed search.
source_text: I sought among them a man conducting himself rightly and standing wholly before Me at the land’s time, so that I would not utterly wipe her out, but I found none.

target_units.text: Run through Jerusalem’s streets and see and learn, and search her squares: if you find a man, if there is one doing justice and seeking faithfulness, then I will be merciful to them, says the Lord.

relationship: contrast between no suitable person found and Moses' successful intervention
rationale: Ezekiel says no person was found standing wholly before God to prevent destruction. The psalm names Moses standing in the breach to turn God's anger away from destruction. The breach belongs to the target; the source is not rewritten with hedge-or-gap wording.
source_text: I sought among them a man conducting himself rightly and standing wholly before Me at the land’s time, so that I would not utterly wipe her out, but I found none.

target_units.text: He said He would destroy them, had not Moses His chosen one stood in the breach before Him, to turn His anger away so He would not destroy.

relationship: close bringing of the people's own ways upon their heads
rationale: Ezekiel's conclusion joins divine wrath with returning their ways upon their heads. The earlier Jerusalem judgment likewise says God has brought their ways upon their heads and will not spare. The source additionally expresses wrath through consuming fire.
source_text: I poured My wrath upon her in the fire of My anger to bring an end. I brought their ways upon their own heads, says the Lord, the Lord.’”

target_units.text: My eye will not spare, nor will I have mercy. I have brought their ways upon their heads.”

relationship: related female family imagery for the cities
rationale: The source introduces two women from one mother, identified as cities in the following explanation. The earlier Jerusalem oracle uses mother, daughter and sister language to expose related wrongdoing. The comparison concerns the familial allegory rather than literal human genealogy.
source_text: “Son of man, there were two women, daughters of one mother,

target_units.text: These are all the things they said against you in a proverb, saying, ‘As the mother, so the daughter.’

You are the daughter of your mother, who rejected her husband and her children, and the sister of your sisters, who rejected their husbands and children. Your mother was a Hittite, and your father an Amorite.

relationship: related recollection of unfaithfulness in Egypt
rationale: The two women's youthful prostitution is placed in Egypt. The preceding historical indictment recalls refusal to abandon Egyptian practices and abominations. The source's sexualized portrayal of the cities differs from the historical statement about Jacob's house.
source_text: and they prostituted themselves in Egypt in their youth. There their breasts fell; there they were deflowered.

target_units.text: I said to them, “Let each cast away the abominations of his eyes, and do not be defiled by Egypt’s practices. I am the Lord your God.”

They revolted from Me and would not listen to Me. They did not cast away the abominations of their eyes or abandon Egypt’s practices. I said I would pour My wrath upon them and complete My anger in them in the midst of Egypt’s land.

relationship: close personification of Samaria as Jerusalem's elder sister
rationale: The source explicitly identifies Oholah with Samaria and Oholibah with Jerusalem. The earlier oracle addressed to Jerusalem calls Samaria the elder sister, also naming Sodom as another sister. That additional figure is not inserted into this source's two-woman story.
source_text: Their names were Oholah the elder and Oholibah her sister. They became Mine and bore sons and daughters. Their names: Samaria is Oholah, and Jerusalem is Oholibah.

target_units.text: Your elder sister is Samaria, she and her daughters, dwelling at your left; your sister younger than you, dwelling at your right, is Sodom and her daughters.

relationship: related turning toward Assyria within an indictment of Israel
rationale: Oholah, identified as Samaria, desires her Assyrian lovers. Hosea describes Israel among the nations and going up to the Assyrians, also naming Ephraim and love of gifts. The target does not use the source's lovers wording or identify a literal woman.
source_text: Oholah prostituted herself away from Me and set her desire upon her lovers, the Assyrians approaching her,

target_units.text: Israel was swallowed up; now he became among the nations like a useless vessel.
Because they went up to the Assyrians; Ephraim flourished by himself, and they loved gifts.
Therefore they will be handed over among the nations. Now I will receive them, and they will pause a little from anointing a king and rulers.

relationship: same-chapter parallel descriptions of desired Assyrian horsemen
rationale: Oholah's Assyrian objects of desire are leaders, generals, choice young men and mounted horsemen. The description of Oholibah's desired Assyrians repeats those categories. The clothing descriptions differ and are not made identical.
source_text: clothed in blue-purple, leaders and generals; all choice young men, horsemen riding horses.

target_units.text: She set her desire upon Assyrians’ sons, leaders and generals near her, clothed in finely bordered garments, horsemen riding horses; all choice young men.

relationship: related Assyrian prostitution in distinct city personifications
rationale: Samaria's female figure bestows prostitution on Assyrians' sons and becomes defiled. The earlier Jerusalem oracle describes prostitution with Assyria's daughters and continued dissatisfaction. The different personified cities and the sons-versus-daughters wording are preserved.
source_text: She bestowed her prostitution upon them, all choice sons of Assyrians; and with all upon whom she set her desire, in all her reflections she was defiled.

target_units.text: You prostituted yourself with the daughters of Assyria, and not even so were you filled; you prostituted yourself, and were not filled.

relationship: related failure to abandon prior Egyptian practices
rationale: Oholah does not abandon the prostitution associated with her youth in Egypt. The earlier historical recital likewise says the people failed to abandon Egypt's practices despite God's command. The target uses the language of rebellion and practices rather than this sexual allegory.
source_text: She did not abandon her prostitution from Egypt, for they lay with her in her youth; they deflowered her and poured their prostitution upon her.

target_units.text: They revolted from Me and would not listen to Me. They did not cast away the abominations of their eyes or abandon Egypt’s practices. I said I would pour My wrath upon them and complete My anger in them in the midst of Egypt’s land.

relationship: related handing of Samaria into Assyrian power
rationale: God hands Oholah, explicitly Samaria, into the Assyrians' hands. Kings narrates the Assyrian siege and capture of Samaria and deportation of Israel. The narrative does not describe the Assyrians as her lovers, which belongs to Ezekiel's interpretation.
source_text: Therefore I handed her into her lovers’ hands, into the hands of Assyrians’ sons, upon whom she had set her desire.

target_units.text: The king of the Assyrians went up through the whole land, went up to Samaria, and besieged it for three years.
In Hoshea’s ninth year the king of the Assyrians captured Samaria and deported Israel to the Assyrians. He settled them in Alae and Abor, rivers of Gozan, and Ore of the Medes.

relationship: related exposure of an unfaithful mother and threatened treatment of her children
rationale: Ezekiel describes uncovering the woman's shame, taking her children and killing her. Hosea threatens stripping the mother naked and withholding mercy from her children. The targets of the explicit killing, taking and withheld mercy remain distinct.
source_text: They uncovered her shame, took her sons and daughters, and killed her with the sword. She became a subject of talk among women, and they inflicted punishments upon her, upon the daughters.

target_units.text: so that I may strip her naked and restore her as on the day of her birth. I will make her like a wilderness, set her like a waterless land and kill her with thirst.
I will certainly show no mercy to her children, for they are children of prostitution.

relationship: close failure of Judah to learn from Israel's prior unfaithfulness
rationale: Oholibah sees her sister's fate and exceeds her corruption. Jeremiah recounts Israel's dismissal and Judah's failure to fear and concludes that Israel is justified in comparison with faithless Judah. The comparison follows the source's named city identities without importing an additional literal family history.
source_text: Her sister Oholibah saw this and corrupted her desire beyond hers, and her prostitution beyond her sister’s prostitution.

target_units.text: I saw that, concerning all the things in which the dwelling of Israel was caught committing adultery, I sent her away and gave a certificate of divorce into her hands. Yet faithless Judah did not fear; she too went and prostituted herself.
Her prostitution came to be regarded as nothing, and she committed adultery with wood and stone.
In all these things faithless Judah did not return to Me with her whole heart, but in falsehood.
The Lord said to me, Israel has justified himself in comparison with faithless Judah.

relationship: same-chapter repetition of attraction to Assyrian officers and cavalry
rationale: Oholibah desires Assyrian leaders, generals and choice young horsemen, echoing the earlier description of Oholah's lovers. The repetition makes the shared course explicit, while finely bordered garments here are not renamed the earlier blue-purple clothing.
source_text: She set her desire upon Assyrians’ sons, leaders and generals near her, clothed in finely bordered garments, horsemen riding horses; all choice young men.

target_units.text: clothed in blue-purple, leaders and generals; all choice young men, horsemen riding horses.

relationship: related comparison of Jerusalem's and Samaria's corrupt ways
rationale: God says the two women share one defiled way. The earlier city oracle compares Jerusalem and Samaria, saying Jerusalem's multiplied lawlessness exceeds Samaria's. The target states a difference of degree rather than denying their common wrongdoing.
source_text: I saw that she was defiled; one way for the two.

target_units.text: Samaria did not sin half your sins. You multiplied your lawlessness beyond theirs and justified your sisters by all the lawlessness you committed.

relationship: close conjunction of prostitution and distant embassies
rationale: Oholibah desires the depicted Chaldeans and sends messengers to their land. Isaiah likewise joins multiplied prostitution and lovers with ambassadors sent beyond the boundaries. The target does not name the Chaldeans or describe their portraits.
source_text: She set her desire upon them at the sight of her eyes and sent messengers to them in the Chaldeans’ land.

target_units.text: Behind your doorposts you set your memorials. You thought that if you departed from Me you would have something more. You loved those sleeping with you
and multiplied your prostitution with them. You increased the number of those far away from you, sent ambassadors beyond your boundaries, turned away, and were humbled as far as Hades.

relationship: related unfaithful involvement with Chaldea
rationale: Babylon's sons come to the woman and defile her, after her message to Chaldea. The earlier Jerusalem oracle describes multiplied covenants toward the Chaldeans' land. It supplies covenant language rather than the source's bed-of-lodgers image or subsequent withdrawal.
source_text: Babylon’s sons came to her, to a bed of lodgers, and defiled her in her prostitution. She was defiled by them, and her soul withdrew from them.

target_units.text: You multiplied your covenants toward the Chaldeans’ land, and not even with these were you filled.

relationship: related divine rejection expressed in terms of God's soul
rationale: God says His soul withdrew from the woman as from her sister. Leviticus warns that His soul will be indignant with the disobedient people amid destruction of their idols. Withdrawal and indignation are related responses, not identical verbs or stages.
source_text: She uncovered her prostitution and uncovered her shame. My soul withdrew from her, as My soul had withdrawn from her sister.

target_units.text: And I will lay waste your pillars, and destroy your wooden images made by hand, and place your limbs upon the limbs of your idols; and My soul shall be indignant with you;

relationship: related prostitution with Egypt in Jerusalem's allegory
rationale: Oholibah recalls youthful prostitution in Egypt. The earlier Jerusalem oracle likewise names prostitution with Egypt's sons. The target describes them as neighbors and does not explicitly place that act in infancy or youth.
source_text: You multiplied your prostitution to recall the days of your youth, in which you prostituted yourself in Egypt,

target_units.text: You prostituted yourself with the sons of Egypt, your neighbors great in flesh, and prostituted yourself in many ways to anger Me.

relationship: related sexualized descriptions of foreign involvement with different nations
rationale: The source compares the desired Chaldeans' flesh and genitals with animals. The earlier oracle describes Egypt's sons as great in flesh. The bodily imagery is related, while the source's Chaldeans are expressly not renamed Egyptians.
source_text: and you set your desire upon the Chaldeans, whose flesh was like donkeys’ and whose genitals were horses’ genitals.

target_units.text: You prostituted yourself with the sons of Egypt, your neighbors great in flesh, and prostituted yourself in many ways to anger Me.

relationship: same-chapter parallel return to the sisters' Egyptian past
rationale: Oholibah revisits the lawlessness of her youth in Egypt. Earlier Oholah is said not to have abandoned her Egyptian prostitution. The parallel concerns the two sisters' persistent past, not an assertion that the same named human woman appears in both units.
source_text: You revisited the lawlessness of your youth, what you did in Egypt at your lodging, where your youthful breasts were.

target_units.text: She did not abandon her prostitution from Egypt, for they lay with her in her youth; they deflowered her and poured their prostitution upon her.

relationship: close reversal in which former lovers are gathered against Jerusalem
rationale: God rouses Oholibah's former lovers and brings them against her from all around. The earlier Jerusalem oracle likewise gathers lovers, both loved and hated, against the city. The former objects of desire becoming instruments of exposure is the particular common reversal.
source_text: Therefore, Oholibah, thus says the Lord: Behold, I am rousing your lovers against you, those from whom your soul withdrew. I will bring them against you all around:

target_units.text: Therefore behold, I am gathering against you all your lovers with whom you mingled, all whom you loved together with all whom you hated. I will gather them against you from all around, reveal your evils to them, and they will see all your shame.

relationship: close northern army with mounted forces directed against Zion
rationale: The source describes a northern force with chariots and peoples surrounding the woman identified as Jerusalem. Jeremiah likewise announces a northern people advancing with horses and chariots against Zion. The target does not reproduce the source's shields or delegated judgments.
source_text: All will come against you from the north: chariots and wheels with a multitude of peoples, large shields and small shields; they will set a guard against you all around. I will set judgment before them, and they will punish you by their judgments.

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord: Behold, a people comes from the north, and nations will be roused from the earth’s extremity.
They will grasp bow and spear; it is ruthless and will show no mercy. Its voice is like a surging sea; on horses and chariots it will draw up like fire for war against you, daughter of Zion.

relationship: close jealousy and wrath in judgment of the unfaithful city
rationale: God announces jealousy and fierce anger followed by mutilation, captivity and killing. The earlier Jerusalem oracle likewise associates retribution for adultery and bloodshed with wrath and jealousy. Its selected unit does not specify removal of nose and ears or the taking of children.
source_text: I will set My jealousy within you, and they will deal with you in fierce anger. They will remove your nose and ears and strike down your remaining people with the sword. They will take your sons and daughters, and fire will consume your remaining people.

target_units.text: I will exact retribution upon you with the retribution of an adulteress and a woman shedding blood, and place you in blood of wrath and jealousy.

relationship: close stripping of clothing and objects of boasting
rationale: Both city judgments say the adversaries will strip the woman's clothing and take her objects or vessels of boasting. The earlier oracle additionally names demolition of the brothel and platform and exposure of nakedness.
source_text: They will strip you of your clothing and take the objects of your boasting.

target_units.text: I will hand you into their hands. They will tear down your brothel, pull down your platform, strip your clothing from you, take your vessels of boasting, and leave you naked and exposed.

relationship: close announced ending of the city's prostitution
rationale: God says He will turn away the woman's impieties and Egyptian prostitution. The earlier Jerusalem oracle likewise promises to turn her away from prostitution and stop her payments. The specific end of Egyptian remembrance belongs to this source rather than that target.
source_text: I will turn your impieties away from you and your prostitution from Egypt’s land. You certainly will not lift your eyes toward them, and you certainly will no longer remember Egypt.

target_units.text: They will burn your houses with fire and exact retributions upon you before many women. I will turn you away from your prostitution, and you certainly will give no more payments.

relationship: related former objects of attachment now hated and brought against the city
rationale: God hands the woman to those she hates and from whom her soul withdrew. The earlier oracle gathers against Jerusalem those she loved together with those she hated. The target includes both groups, while the source names the hated group.
source_text: For thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am handing you into the hands of those you hate, those from whom your soul withdrew.

target_units.text: Therefore behold, I am gathering against you all your lovers with whom you mingled, all whom you loved together with all whom you hated. I will gather them against you from all around, reveal your evils to them, and they will see all your shame.

relationship: close plundering and naked exposure of personified Jerusalem
rationale: The hostile agents take the fruit of toil and leave the woman naked with her shame exposed. The earlier oracle likewise takes clothing and prized vessels and leaves Jerusalem naked and exposed. The descriptions of seized property differ.
source_text: They will deal with you in hatred and take all the fruit of your pain and toil. You will be naked and exposed to shame, and the shame of your prostitution and your impiety will be uncovered. Your prostitution

target_units.text: I will hand you into their hands. They will tear down your brothel, pull down your platform, strip your clothing from you, take your vessels of boasting, and leave you naked and exposed.

relationship: close attribution of harm to the people's own abandonment of God
rationale: The source attributes the woman's treatment to her prostitution after nations. Jeremiah asks whether abandoning God brought such things upon the people and says their apostasy will discipline them, in a passage naming Egypt and Assyria. The target does not describe the same attackers or every feature of the woman's punishment.
source_text: did these things to you when you prostituted yourself after nations and were defiled in their reflections.

target_units.text: Has abandoning Me not brought these things upon you? says the Lord your God.
Now what do you have to do with Egypt’s road, to drink Gihon’s water? And what do you have to do with the Assyrians’ road, to drink river waters?
Your apostasy will discipline you, and your evil will rebuke you. Know and see that abandoning Me is bitter for you, says the Lord your God; and I took no pleasure in you, says the Lord your God.

relationship: close judgment-cup imagery applied to Jerusalem
rationale: God places the sister's cup in Jerusalem's hands because she followed that sister's way. Isaiah addresses Jerusalem as having drunk the cup of anger from the Lord's hand. The prior transfer from Samaria belongs to Ezekiel, not the target.
source_text: You walked in your sister’s way; I will put her cup into your hands.

target_units.text: Awake, awake, rise, Jerusalem, you who drank the cup of anger from the Lord’s hand. You drank out and emptied the cup of falling, the bowl of anger.

relationship: related drinking from a divinely assigned judgment cup
rationale: The source announces drinking the sister's deep, wide cup, whose effect continues into the following unit. Jeremiah is given a cup of unmixed wine for the nations, bringing vomiting and madness before the sword. The source's stated dimensions and the target's explicit wine are not made identical.
source_text: Thus says the Lord: You will drink your sister’s cup, deep and wide, abounding to bring about

target_units.text: Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: Take this cup of unmixed wine from My hand, and give it to all the nations to whom I send you to drink,
and they will drink, vomit, and go mad before the sword I am sending among them.

relationship: close collapse and drunkenness associated with Jerusalem's judgment cup
rationale: The source names drunkenness, collapse and Samaria's cup of annihilation. Isaiah describes Jerusalem's cup of falling and anger and calls her drunk but not from wine. The target does not identify the cup as Samaria's.
source_text: drunkenness; you will be filled with collapse. And the cup of annihilation, your sister Samaria’s cup—

target_units.text: Awake, awake, rise, Jerusalem, you who drank the cup of anger from the Lord’s hand. You drank out and emptied the cup of falling, the bowl of anger.
There was no one to comfort you among all your children you bore, and no one to take your hand among all your sons you raised.
These two confront you—who will grieve with you?—fall and crushing, famine and sword. Who will comfort you?
Your sons are helpless, sleeping at every way out like a half-boiled beet, full of the Lord’s anger, exhausted because of the Lord God.
Therefore listen, humbled one, drunk but not from wine.

relationship: close removal of festivals and new moons from the unfaithful female figure
rationale: Ezekiel says God will turn away her festivals and new moons. Hosea likewise removes the woman's rejoicings, festivals, new moons, Sabbaths and assemblies. This follows the actual festival clause rather than substituting a different edition's cup-shard imagery.
source_text: you will drink it. I will turn away her festivals and her new moons, for I have spoken, says the Lord.

target_units.text: I will turn away all her rejoicings, her festivals, new moons and Sabbaths, and all her festal assemblies.

relationship: related forgetting of God within feminine imagery of unfaithfulness
rationale: Ezekiel charges forgetting God and casting Him behind the body. Jeremiah contrasts the expected remembrance of bridal adornment with God's people forgetting Him for countless days. The target supports the forgetting charge but does not repeat the source's body clause.
source_text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Because you forgot Me and cast Me behind your body, you too must take your impiety and your prostitution.”

target_units.text: Will a bride forget her adornment, or a virgin her breastband? Yet My people forgot Me for days beyond counting.

relationship: parallel commission to expose the cities' lawlessness
rationale: Ezekiel is commanded to declare Oholah's and Oholibah's lawless deeds. The earlier oracle begins with a command to testify to Jerusalem's lawlessness before its female personification. The source addresses two named city figures rather than Jerusalem alone.
source_text: The Lord said to me, “Son of man, will you not judge Oholah and Oholibah? Declare their lawless deeds to them,

target_units.text: “Son of man, solemnly testify to Jerusalem about her lawlessness,

relationship: close condemnation of children offered through fire
rationale: Ezekiel accuses the women of making children borne to God pass through fire offerings. Jeremiah condemns Judah's burning sons and daughters at Topheth, an act God did not command. The target names the location; the source explicitly stresses that the children were borne to God.
source_text: for they committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. They committed adultery with their reflections, and made their children whom they bore to Me pass through fire offerings for them.

target_units.text: For Judah’s sons did evil before Me, says the Lord; they set their abominations in the house over which My name has been called, to defile it.
And they built Topheth’s altar, which is in the ravine of the son of Hinnom, to burn up their sons and daughters in fire, which I did not command them and did not conceive in My heart.

relationship: close inverse of reverence for holy things and Sabbath observance
rationale: Ezekiel accuses the women of defiling holy things and profaning Sabbaths. Leviticus commands keeping God's Sabbaths and revering His holy things. Both named duties are violated in the source.
source_text: They even did these things to Me: they defiled My holy things and profaned My Sabbaths.

target_units.text: You shall keep My Sabbaths and revere My holy things. I am the Lord.

relationship: close conjunction of grave offenses with entry into God's house
rationale: The source describes slaughtering children for idols and then entering God's holy places. Jeremiah likewise lists murder, adultery and foreign worship followed by standing in the house bearing God's name. The shared sequence does not make Jeremiah's murder clause explicitly child sacrifice.
source_text: When they slaughtered their children for their idols, they entered My holy places to profane them. Indeed, they acted this way within My house.

target_units.text: and murder and commit adultery and steal and swear unjustly, and you burned incense to Baal and followed foreign gods whom you do not know, to your own harm,
and you came and stood before Me in the house over which My name has been called and said, ‘We have kept away, so as not to do all these abominations,’
is My house, over which My name has been called there, a robbers’ cave before you? And behold, I have seen, says the Lord.

relationship: close adornment with ornaments and antimony eye paint in a city oracle
rationale: The woman bathes, paints her eyes with antimony and adorns herself for distant visitors. Jeremiah describes scarlet, golden ornaments and antimony eye paint as futile when lovers reject the addressed city. Bathing and messengers are not supplied by the target.
source_text: Indeed, for the men coming from far away, to whom they sent messengers—as soon as they arrived, you immediately bathed, painted your eyes with antimony and adorned yourself with ornaments,

target_units.text: And you, what will you do if you put on scarlet and adorn yourself with golden ornaments, and if you paint your eyes with antimony? Your adornment is in vain; your lovers have rejected you; they seek your soul.

relationship: close misuse of the oil and incense claimed by God
rationale: The source identifies the incense and oil as God's and says they delighted in them beside the adorned table and couch. The earlier oracle likewise calls the oil and incense God's and says the woman set them before her images. The source's delight is not rewritten as the target's precise placing action.
source_text: and sat upon a spread couch with an adorned table before it. My incense and My oil—they delighted in them.
