target_units.text: You took your patterned clothing and clothed them; you set My oil and My incense before them.

relationship: close bracelets-and-crown adornment language with differing participants
rationale: The source describes bracelets for hands and a crown of boasting for heads amid arriving men and celebration. In the earlier oracle God adorns Jerusalem with bracelets and a crown of boasting. The shared objects and body locations do not resolve the source's pronouns into the target's named giver and recipient.
source_text: They struck up a harmonious sound. With men arriving from the mass of people out of the wilderness, they gave bracelets for their hands and a crown of boasting upon their heads.

target_units.text: and adorned you with ornaments, placed bracelets around your hands and a necklace around your neck,
and put a ring around your nostril, little hoops upon your ears and a crown of boasting upon your head.

relationship: related legal category of punishment for adultery
rationale: The city figures are to receive the punishment of an adulteress from righteous men. Leviticus prescribes punishment for adultery with another man's wife. The source applies this legal category within its city allegory rather than narrating that individual legal case.
source_text: Righteous men will punish them with the punishment of an adulteress and the punishment of bloodshed, for they are adulteresses, and blood is on their hands.

target_units.text: If a man commits adultery with a man’s wife, or commits adultery with his neighbour’s wife, both the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.

relationship: related accountability for human bloodshed
rationale: The source says the women have blood on their hands and will receive punishment for bloodshed. Genesis declares an accounting for human life and reciprocal bloodshed for one who sheds human blood. It supports this distinct bloodshed charge rather than the source's adultery category.
source_text: Righteous men will punish them with the punishment of an adulteress and the punishment of bloodshed, for they are adulteresses, and blood is on their hands.

target_units.text: “And surely I will require your blood, the blood of your lives. From every beast I will require it, and from the hand of a fellow man I will require the life of man.
Whoever sheds the blood of man, his own blood shall be shed in return; for in the image of God I made man.

relationship: close assembling of a crowd against the personified city
rationale: God commands a multitude against the women with turmoil and plunder. The earlier Jerusalem judgment likewise brings crowds against her, followed by stones and swords. The selected target does not expressly repeat the source's plunder word.
source_text: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Bring a multitude against them and set turmoil and plunder among them,

target_units.text: They will bring crowds against you, stone you with stones, and slaughter you with their swords.

relationship: close cluster of stones, swords and burned houses in the city judgment
rationale: Both descriptions combine the crowd's stones, swords and burning houses. This source additionally says sons and daughters will be killed. That explicit fate is not assigned to the target's children merely because children occur elsewhere in its oracle.
source_text: and stone them with the multitude’s stones and pierce them with their swords. They will kill their sons and daughters and burn their houses.

target_units.text: They will bring crowds against you, stone you with stones, and slaughter you with their swords.
They will burn your houses with fire and exact retributions upon you before many women. I will turn you away from your prostitution, and you certainly will give no more payments.

relationship: related punitive example intended to prevent repetition of wrongdoing
rationale: Ezekiel says the women will be disciplined after the removal of impiety and will not repeat the acts. Deuteronomy gives a punishment for enticing others to foreign gods and says Israel will hear, fear and not repeat such evil. The offenses, subjects and stated responses are distinct, while deterrence is explicit in both.
source_text: I will turn impiety away from the land. All women will be disciplined and certainly will not act according to their impieties.

target_units.text: And they shall stone him with stones, and he shall die; for he sought to turn you away from the Lord your God, who brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
And all Israel shall hear and fear, and shall no more do such an evil thing among you.

relationship: close return of the city figure's own wrongdoing upon herself
rationale: The source says the women's impiety will be brought upon them and they will receive their sins. The earlier oracle likewise says God has brought Jerusalem's ways upon her head. The source adds recognition of the Lord rather than repeating the target's infancy-memory accusation.
source_text: Your impiety will be brought upon you, and you will receive the sins of your reflections. You will know that I am the Lord.”

target_units.text: Because you did not remember the day of your infancy but grieved Me with all these things, behold, I have brought your ways upon your head, says the Lord. Thus you committed impiety in addition to all your lawlessness.

relationship: close matching date at the beginning of Jerusalem's siege
rationale: Ezekiel dates this word to the ninth year, tenth month and tenth day. Jeremiah records Babylon's arrival against Jerusalem on that same numbered year, month and day. The source's next unit explicitly connects its date with the siege.
source_text: The Lord’s word came to me in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, saying,

target_units.text: In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his force came against Jerusalem. They enclosed her with a palisade and built around her with squared stones.

relationship: related onset of Babylon's pressure against Jerusalem
rationale: Ezekiel is told to record the day Babylon's king presses against Jerusalem. Kings records Babylon's king coming with his force and constructing an enclosing wall. Kings gives the ninth year and tenth month here but does not give the tenth day supplied by Ezekiel and Jeremiah.
source_text: “Son of man, write for yourself a record of the day, from this day on which Babylon’s king pressed against Jerusalem, from this present day,

target_units.text: In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon came with all his force against Jerusalem. He camped against it and built an enclosing wall against it all around.

relationship: close cauldron-and-meat imagery concerning Jerusalem
rationale: The commanded parable begins by setting on a cauldron, developed as the city in the following units. The earlier oracle quotes the city's leaders calling it a cauldron and themselves its meat, then identifies their dead as the meat. The different speakers and interpretations remain explicit.
source_text: and speak a parable against the provoking house. Say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: Set on the cauldron and pour water into it,

target_units.text: who say, ‘Have the houses not been built recently? She is the cauldron, and we are the meat.’
Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, son of man.”
The Lord’s spirit fell upon me, and He said to me, “Say, ‘Thus says the Lord: You have said this, house of Israel, and I understand the deliberations of your spirit.
You have multiplied your dead in this city and filled her roads with the wounded.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Your dead whom you struck within her are the meat, and she is the cauldron; but I will bring you out of her.

relationship: related flesh-and-bones cooking imagery for a community's harm
rationale: Ezekiel puts selected cuts, stripped from bones, into the cauldron. Micah depicts oppressive authorities taking flesh from bones and dividing the people like meat for a cooking pot. The source's divine judgment sign differs from the target's accusation against exploitative rulers.
source_text: and put the cut pieces into it, every good cut, leg and shoulder stripped from the bones,

target_units.text: you who hate good things and seek evil things, who snatch their skins from them and their flesh from their bones?”
Just as they ate the flesh of My people, flayed their skins from their bones, crushed their bones and divided them into pieces like flesh for a cauldron and meat for a cooking pot,

relationship: related bones and meat within a cooking-pot image
rationale: The source burns bones beneath the choice pieces and speaks of bones cooked within. Micah depicts crushed bones and divided flesh as meat for a pot. The target does not say the bones are fuel beneath it, and its actors are the oppressive authorities.
source_text: from choice animals taken. Burn the bones beneath them. It boiled, it boiled, and her bones have been cooked within her.

target_units.text: Just as they ate the flesh of My people, flayed their skins from their bones, crushed their bones and divided them into pieces like flesh for a cauldron and meat for a cooking pot,

relationship: related failed removal of corruption through metalworking imagery
rationale: The city is a cauldron whose rust has not come out. Jeremiah describes vain silverworking in which wickedness was not melted away and the people are rejected silver. The rusted vessel and the unsuccessfully worked silver are different images of persistent corruption.
source_text: Therefore thus says the Lord: O city of bloodshed! A cauldron with rust in it, whose rust has not come out of her! He brought it out limb by limb; no lot fell upon her.

target_units.text: The bellows failed from the fire; the lead failed. In vain the silversmith works silver; their wickedness was not melted away.
Call them rejected silver, because the Lord rejected them.

relationship: related blood remaining uncovered on the earth
rationale: God says He has set the city's blood on smooth rock rather than covering it with earth. Job asks the earth not to cover the blood of his flesh. The speakers, ownership of the blood and smooth-rock detail differ; Job's plea is not made the city's action.
source_text: For her blood is within her. I have set it upon smooth rock; I have not poured it upon the earth to cover it with earth.

target_units.text: Earth, do not cover the blood of my flesh, and let there be no place for my cry!

relationship: close uncovered blood associated with divine wrath
rationale: God leaves the blood uncovered to bring wrath and vengeance. Isaiah likewise joins the Lord's wrath with the earth uncovering blood and not covering the killed. The source expressly assigns placement on the rock to God, while Isaiah describes the earth uncovering it.
source_text: To make wrath rise for vengeance to be exacted, I have set her blood upon smooth rock so that it will not be covered.

target_units.text: Go, My people, enter your inner rooms, shut your door, hide for a little, a very little while, until the Lord’s wrath passes.
For behold, the Lord brings wrath from the holy place upon those dwelling on the earth. The earth will uncover its blood and will not cover those killed.

relationship: related heated-cauldron imagery for coming judgment
rationale: The parable calls for more wood and fire until flesh melts and broth is reduced. Jeremiah sees a cauldron heated from beneath and is told of northern calamities and judgment. The target's vision does not supply Ezekiel's meat, bones or reduced broth.
source_text: and multiply the wood and kindle the fire, so that the flesh melts and the broth is reduced,

target_units.text: The Lord’s word came to me a second time, saying, What do you see? I said, A cauldron heated from beneath, its face away from the north.
The Lord said to me, From the north calamities will be kindled upon all who inhabit the land.

Because behold, I am summoning all the kingdoms from the north of the land, says the Lord. They will come and each set his throne at the forecourts of Jerusalem’s gates, against all her surrounding walls and against all Judah’s cities.
I will speak to them with judgment concerning all their evil, because they abandoned Me, sacrificed to foreign gods and bowed down to the works of their hands.

relationship: related heated metal and removal of uncleanness
rationale: The cauldron's copper is heated and melts amid uncleanness so that its rust ceases. Malachi describes smelting and purifying silver and gold as an image for cleansing the sons of Levi. The metals and groups differ, and the following source unit complicates the anticipated removal by saying rust persists.
source_text: and it stands upon the coals, so that its copper is scorched and heated and melts amid its uncleanness, and its rust ceases,

target_units.text: And who will endure the day of his entrance? Or who will stand at his appearance? For he enters like a smelting fire and like launderers’ herb.

He will sit, smelting and purifying as with silver and gold. He will cleanse the sons of Levi and melt them like gold and silver, and they will be those who bring a sacrifice to the Lord in righteousness.

relationship: close failure to remove corruption despite the heated process
rationale: Ezekiel says the abundant rust will not leave the cauldron. Jeremiah describes failed bellows and lead, with silver worked in vain because wickedness was not melted away. Both preserve the failure rather than claiming successful purification.
source_text: yet her abundant rust certainly will not leave her; her rust will be put to shame,

target_units.text: The bellows failed from the fire; the lead failed. In vain the silversmith works silver; their wickedness was not melted away.

relationship: related cleansing linked with divine judgment
rationale: Ezekiel asks about not being cleansed until God's wrath is filled up. Isaiah promises cleansing of Zion's filth and blood through a spirit of judgment and burning. The question and threatened delay in the source are distinguished from the target's positive promise.
source_text: because you were being defiled. And what if you are not cleansed any more until I fill up My wrath?

target_units.text: because the Lord will wash away the filth of Zion’s sons and daughters and thoroughly cleanse the blood from their midst, by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.

relationship: close judgment according to conduct without sparing
rationale: God says He will act, not draw back or show mercy, and judge the city according to its ways and bloodshed. The earlier oracle likewise combines wrath, judgment according to ways and refusal to spare or show mercy. Both assign the consequences to the people's own acts.
source_text: I, the Lord, have spoken, and it will come, and I will act. I will not draw back, nor will I show mercy. According to your ways and your reflections I will judge you, says the Lord. Therefore I will judge you according to your bloodshed, and according to your reflections I will judge you, the unclean one, the famous one, abundant in provoking.’”

target_units.text: Now soon I will pour My anger upon you and complete My wrath in you; I will judge you in your ways and bring all your abominations upon you.
My eye will not spare, nor will I have mercy; I will bring your ways upon you, and your abominations will be in your midst. You will recognize that I am the Lord who strikes.
Now the end is upon you. I Myself will send against you and exact retribution upon you in your ways; I will bring all your abominations upon you.
My eye will not spare you, nor will I have mercy; I will bring your way upon you, and your abominations will be in your midst. You will recognize that I am the Lord.

relationship: related prophetic prohibition of customary mourning during announced judgment
rationale: God says He will take the desires of Ezekiel's eyes in battle array and forbids breast-beating or being wept over. Jeremiah is likewise forbidden to join the people's mourning because God removed His peace. The source's battle-array wording and passive being-wept-over wording are preserved.
source_text: “Son of man, behold, I am taking the desires of your eyes from you in battle array. You certainly will not beat your breast, nor be wept over.

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord: Do not enter their gathering or go to beat yourself in mourning, and do not mourn them, because I have removed My peace from this people.
